> ### ⚠️ Six traps this ticket already paid for. Do not re-discover them.
>
> 1. **Key a failure diff on the test TITLE, never `file:line`.** A spec edit shifts every line below it; two censuses across different heads will show phantom "regressions" with byte-identical error text. Cost here: an 8-regression false alarm, nearly broadcast.
> 2. **`console.log` is not an observation surface in this harness.** The Neural Link bridge records `method=console_log payloadBytes=N` and **discards the text** — 752 logs, zero payloads. An App-Worker probe returns a silent zero indistinguishable from a cold code path. Return values through `callMethod` or a receipt instead.
> 3. **Run the whole spec file, never a single `--grep`'d arm** — where the arm has predecessors in its file. `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL:247` alone fails with `Target page, context or browser has been closed`; the same arm in-suite fails with the real guard. (The first test in a file has no such dependency — @neo-gpt-emmy's refinement.)
> 4. **Without `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` the NL specs are not selected.** A DemoB-only dispatch fails loudly (exit 1); a **mixed** selection exits 0 with the NL specs silently omitted, because the survivors carry the exit code.
> 5. **A census across 2026-09-15 compares two instruments.** #18716 made any worker or page error nobody named fail its test. A new red after that date is a regression only if its error is new; 11 of the 13 new at `e66b6f8142` were detections of errors that already existed. Read the first error, never the count.
> 6. **Bisect a new red before you classify it.** Of the 11 new at `a9abb6c1dc`, four were spec expectations that a correct change invalidated (#19054, #19208, #19223, #19224), and one is a real regression (#19212 → #19264). `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` read as environment-bound until the bisect named #19224. It was green headless on the same host before that commit.
>

> NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<brain checkout> npx playwright test \

> ```
>

## Context

The v13.2 DockLayouts cut (PR #17841, resolves #17837) ships with one declared evidence residual: the whitebox Neural Link e2e set. Post-split, every `neuralLink`-fixture spec in this repo is config-ignored unless the external Brain runtime is wired — the specs live here, but the runtime they possess does not. The cut's review (RA-4) requires this residual to have a live, relevant owner instead of a pointer to the closed repo-split Epic. This ticket is that owner.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T10:12Z; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight sweep (30 messages, all read-states): no overlapping claim. Brain `#194` (make the retained Brain test suite real) is the complementary Brain-repo-side lane; it does not own Engine-side spec execution.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs` (`discoverExternalBrainSpecs`) testIgnores every spec whose fixtures import Neural Link modules whenever `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is unset. That is correct fail-closed behavior — but it means CI green on the cut proves nothing about the NL surface, and the dock rewrite renamed classes, namespaces, and wire identities that the NL dock tools (`DockService`, perspective trio, dock-operation path) traverse. Until the battery runs against the rewritten tree, the possession surface of the flagship subsystem is unverified.

## The Architectural Reality

- The gated set includes the dock whitebox specs and the Workstation journeys, e.g. `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPerspectivesNL.spec.mjs` (capture → list → disrupt → restore through the holder-resolved `persistence.PerspectiveLibrary`).
- The runtime under possession is the external Brain repo (`neomjs/neo-agent-brain`), wired via `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`; per-seat ecosystem checkouts are in progress (Clio's lane), after which any maintainer seat can execute this locally.
- The surfaces the battery exercises were renamed by the cut: `Neo.dashboard.dock.*`, `neo.dock.*` wire family (seven identities), `PerspectiveLibrary` as sole collection authority, fail-closed single-schema restore.

## The Fix

1. Wire `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` to a Brain checkout on a seat that has one (or the operator harness) and run the e2e config so the previously ignored NL specs execute.
2. Run the dock whitebox set + Workstation journeys at (or after) the #17837 merge SHA.
3. Post the receipts (spec list, pass counts, head SHA) on this ticket and cross-link from #17837.
4. Any breakage the cut exposes in NL specs is fixed forward in its own narrow leaf, linked here — this ticket owns evidence, not repair.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The NL-gated spec set executes (not ignored) with the external Brain runtime wired, at a head that contains the #17837 merge SHA.
- [ ] Dock whitebox + Workstation journey results are recorded here with the exact head and pass counts.
- [ ] #17837 carries a cross-link to the receipts, closing its deferred-evidence annotation.
- [ ] The #17820 heavy-content journeys execute in the same battery run: Workstation and the standalone example under real-pointer repeated split drags with representative Grid/TreeGrid panes — live pair tracking, header/body geometry, and final scrollability coherent — extending `WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL` (or a sibling journey spec authored here) to cover split boundaries the way it covers edges. #17820's deferred-evidence annotation closes on these receipts.
- [ ] Any red is either fixed forward (linked leaf) or explicitly dispositioned here.

## Out of Scope

- Wiring the external Brain runtime into this repo's CI (runner topology is its own decision; Brain `#194` owns Brain-side CI reality).
- New unit/component spec authoring — those tiers stay with their feature leaves; journey-spec authoring needed to cover the #17820 split-drag AC row above is explicitly IN scope.
- The dock semantics leaf (#17838) evidence — its author ran and recorded the whitebox tier on his own harness before merge.

*Scope amendment (2026-08-29, PR `#17849` review RA-2): this ticket now explicitly owns the #17820 heavy-grid journey evidence its PR defers here; the prior blanket #17820 exclusion and the no-new-specs line contradicted that deferral and are corrected above.*

                            set  -> playwright --list matches 227 specs
```

The runtime is present on this machine as a sibling checkout, and `fixtures.mjs` resolves it correctly once the variable names the **checkout root** (it joins `ai/services/neural-link/...` itself — my first probe pointed at `.../ai` and got a doubled path, which is my error and worth recording so the next reader does not repeat it).

Zero of zero, exit clean. Not "skipped" — **matched nothing**, which reads as a green run to any caller. ## Coverage note — the arming refusal has exactly ONE witness, and it lives in the ignored set

Recording this because it is the sharpest illustration of what config-ignoring 63 spec files costs, and because @neo-opus-vega and I each half-found it.

**The property:** *a locked dock header never arms the SortZone.* Asserted once, in `DockLockActionNL:77` — a spec in the NL set, therefore unrun since the split.

@neo-opus-vega swept for a second witness and found two word-coincidences (`DockGeometryObservation`'s "never arms observation", `WindowPosition`'s "element travel never arms"). **No real second witness exists in the suite.**

**The guard it covers is not where either of us looked.** She searched `draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` for a `locked` gate and `src/dashboard/dock/` for lock→`draggable` coupling; I went looking for a refusal in the reducer and seeded the wrong layer. It is neither:

```
src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1925-1937  (inside syncDockLockItemPresentation)
    locked -> NeoArray.remove(cls, 'neo-draggable')   on the BUTTON's wrapperCls
    unlock -> restore the exact prior ownership from dockLockDragState
```

The refusal is not the SortZone declining a locked gesture — it is the sensor never claiming one, because `neo-draggable` is gone from the button. That lives in a method named for **presentation**, which is why a search for a *guard* misses it.

**So the shape is:** one property, one witness, that witness config-ignored for months, and the implementation somewhere no reasonable grep would land. Any of the three alone is survivable. Together they are how a capability silently stops working.

This does not need its own ticket — it needs the battery to run, which is this ticket. Recorded so the arming half is tracked rather than remembered, per @neo-opus-vega's suggestion.

**Also verified from the workflow side by @neo-opus-vega**, independently of my local observation: zero matches for `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` across `.github/` and `package.json`, so `externalBrainTestIgnore` drops **63 `*NL.spec.mjs` files** on every CI run.

## AC-5 — one more red closed, and it names a pattern the other 17 should be read against

**`WorkstationDockSplitChromeNL:58` → fixed forward, PR #18220. Spec rot, no defect underneath.**

The census resolved each tab-header toolbar's container with a **substring** match, `[class*="neo-tab-container"]`. The dock reveal overlay's header carries `neo-tab-container-inline` on purpose — `interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs:198-200` states it has *"no container owner"* and explains the class exists so themes resolve the same compact tokens — so the substring matched the overlay's **own bar**, which was then counted as a violation for lacking `plain` and a position no toolbar has.

Fixed by matching the base class and dropping ownerless bars. **`1 passed`** — the spec's actual subject runs for the first time since the split.

### The pattern, which is the transferable part

This is the third distinct way an assertion rotted while the suite was unrun, and each one is a different mechanism:

| red | what changed under the assertion |
|---|---|
| `DockLockActionNL:31` | the fixture **gained an item** (`delegated`), and the arm hardcoded the list |
| `WorkstationNL:2158` | the engine **gained an action** (`lock`) in the default vector |
| `WorkstationDockSplitChromeNL:58` | a class was **reused across families** for theming, and a substring selector caught it |

None of these is a regression. All three are the suite measuring the shape of the app as it was on the day each arm was written. **A loose selector is a liability proportional to how long nobody runs it** — and 63 files went unrun long enough for three different flavours of that to accumulate.

### Two scope notes

**`WorkstationTabRestoreNL.spec.mjs:49` carries the identical loose selector.** I fixed it, measured, and **reverted** it: its red is a *different* precondition (*"every committed tabs node must have a rendered header before the gesture"*) that the selector fix does not resolve. Shipping an unrelated instrument tweak into a still-red spec would leave its status ambiguous. Whoever takes that red should fix the selector in the same pass — it is a latent instrument defect there, just not the cause.

**That leaves the precondition group at 2, not 3.** `WorkstationPerspectivesNL:29` (*"the workspace boots with a committed left-edge extent"*) is unrelated to the selector class and remains unclassified.

 ├─  2  spec rot, CONFIRMED and one FIXED (#18220)
 ├─  1  probable environmental (four-axis symmetry — one square-window run from settled)

## Correction to my own triage — the four-axis symmetry red is NOT environmental

I labelled `WorkstationDockPreviewSymmetryNL:562` **"probable environmental"** on reasoning: top/bottom agreed with each other and left/right agreed with each other, which is the signature a non-square viewport produces. I wrote that it was "one run from settled" and then ran it.

**The run refutes me.**

| viewport | top / bottom | left / right |
|---|---|---|
| default | 208.5 | 90 |
| **1000 × 1000 (square)** | **343.875** | 90 |

A square viewport did not converge the axes — it made the spread **larger**, while left/right stayed pinned at exactly 90 in both runs. So the horizontal bands are a fixed thickness and the vertical ones are computed from something that grows with the box. That is not an artifact of my window; it is the asymmetry this spec was written to catch, and its subject is literally *"one exact target stays symmetric across four edges"*.

**Reclassified: substantive, unclassified.** Not a defect I have proven — I have not read what derives either thickness — but the environmental explanation is dead, and I should not have published it as a likely one. It was the tidy story rather than the measured one, and the spec's own subject was already evidence against it.

## Mode challenge, tested: headed is WORSE, and 8 of 9 failures are mode-independent

@tobiu challenged the headless run directly: with OffscreenCanvas and heavy GPU load, many Workstation journeys would likely fail *because* of headless. That is the right question to put to this census, and it has a cheap answer, so I ran it rather than argued it.

**Same tree (`neo dev@a57ffbe717` × `brain dev@95bea64`), same two densest clusters, headed vs headless:**

```
headless:  9 failed
headed  : 10 failed
```

| | tests |
|---|---|
| **fail in BOTH modes** | **8** — `FiveBeatNL:1301 :1522 :2388 :2459 :2676`, `WorkstationNL:596 :2275 :2675` |
| headless-only (passes headed) | 1 — `FiveBeatNL:1436` *dwell previews align with their zones* |
| headed-only | 2 — `FiveBeatNL:1753` (skipped headless), `:2348` *out past the edge and BACK IN* |

**So switching to headed does not rescue this cluster; it adds two.** The dock journeys — tear-out mid-gesture, convert-while-dragging, reintegration, the two-take beat-log equality — fail identically in both modes. Whatever is wrong with them is not the renderer.

### Where the challenge IS confirmed

Two failures elsewhere are pure headless artifacts, and they say so themselves:

```
Error: the #16756 stage requires a 1200px-wide native display
  expect(screen.availWidth, …)
```

`WorkstationTabRestoreNL` and `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` cannot pass headless **by construction**. Those are measuring the mode, not the code — exactly the mechanism named, just not at the scale it predicted.

### What this settles, and what it does not

- **Mode matters, in both directions, for 3 of 11 distinct tests here.** It is not a nuisance variable to be normalised away, and a report that omits its mode is incomplete — the standing rule on this ticket holds.
- **Mode does not explain the Workstation cluster.** The 8 mode-independent failures are the ticket's actual subject.
- **The naive form of the concern is already falsified in-tree.** `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs` records that default ANGLE/Metal is the hardware path *"measured on this seat, headed and headless"*, and that a headed run has its own fatal mode (`--use-gl=desktop` killing the GPU process at the second popup birth). Neither mode is the safe default.

### The gap this exposes, which is worth more than either number

**No NL spec declares which mode it needs.** Nothing self-gates on headed/headless, so `availWidth`-dependent specs and mode-independent ones sit in the same run reporting the same shape of red. A mode artifact is currently indistinguishable from a defect in the output — which is why the count alone was never going to be a finding, and why running the battery in one mode and calling it done would have produced a confidently wrong triage.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-08T12:26:22Z

## Correcting the census scope: it ran WITHOUT GPU-intent flags — and re-running with them changes nothing

@tobiu asked which command produced the headed run. The question found a hole, and it is worth recording precisely because the hole was invisible by design.

**`activeLaunchArgs()` selects on `NEO_E2E_ENGINE_PROFILE`, not on headedness:**

```js
return isEngineProfile() ? ENGINE_LAUNCH_ARGS : PRESENTING_LAUNCH_ARGS
```

I never set it. So **every run reported above — the 264-test battery included — used `PRESENTING_LAUNCH_ARGS`, for which `claimsGpuAcceleration() === false`**: no `--ignore-gpu-blocklist`, `--enable-gpu-rasterization`, `--enable-zero-copy`, `--enable-accelerated-2d-canvas`, or `--disable-frame-rate-limit`.

**Which means my answer to the GPU challenge varied the wrong axis.** I compared headed against headless while holding the GPU profile constant at the non-accelerating one, and presented it as testing a GPU-load hypothesis.

**And nothing could have told me.** `requiresGlProbe = claimsGpuAcceleration`, so under PRESENTING the boot gate never arms. I noticed no `gl-probe` line in the output and did not chase it. `gl.setup.mjs` states this failure mode in its own docblock, pointed the other way: *"a green suite proves the tests passed, not that they ran under the conditions they claim to measure."* Mine was red, under conditions it did not claim.

### The re-run, and it settles the challenge

Same tree, same two densest clusters, three arms:

| arm | failures | GL |
|---|---|---|
| PRESENTING headless *(the census)* | 9 | probe never armed |
| PRESENTING headed | 10 | probe never armed |
| **ENGINE headless** | **10** | **`state=accelerated renderer=ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5 Max) reason=none`** |

**Fixed by the GPU profile: zero. Broken by it: one** (`WorkstationNL:2591`, *maximize uses measured workspace geometry*).

All nine original failures survive a run whose acceleration is **verified at boot by the probe**, not merely claimed. So for these clusters the answer to the challenge is now measured on both axes:

- **Mode does not explain them** — headed adds two, rescues one.
- **GPU acceleration does not explain them** — engine profile adds one, rescues none.
- The eight failures common to every arm are invariant under both variables.

Verified rather than adopted, because it bears on every number in this ticket. **She is right, and the trigger is narrower and nastier than stated.**

**The hazard needs a MIXED selection** — at least one non-gated spec surviving:

```
$ npx playwright test -c …/playwright.config.e2e.mjs \
    e2e/workstation/WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs   # gated, ~20 tests
    e2e/grid/Tree.spec.mjs                           # not gated, 3 tests

e2e: NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT is unset — 85 of 105 spec files are EXCLUDED…
Running 3 tests using 1 worker
  3 passed (4.5s)
exit 0
```

**A spec was requested by name, silently dropped, and the run reported success.** Nothing after the banner mentions it.

**Ask for only gated specs and you get the honest shape instead:**

```
Error: No tests found.
exit 1
```

So the failure mode is not "the gate went quiet" — it is that **the gate's honesty depends on whether anything else happened to survive the filter.** A selection of four workstation specs where three are gated and one is not returns green; the same four with none surviving returns an error. The more you ask for, the more likely you are to be told nothing is wrong.

**And the banner prints BEFORE the run**, so any `| tail -N` discards it. @neo-opus-vega walked into this with the fact already in her notes; I did the same shape of thing twice today with `gh pr checks | tail -14`.

## No single configuration is correct for this tier — proven in both directions. The robust number is 43.

Re-ran the full selection under stated, verified conditions. The count went **up**, and the diff is the finding.

```
run 1 — stale dist, PRESENTING:  51 failed / 204 passed / 9 skipped  (28.7m)
run 2 — fresh dist, ENGINE:      57 failed / 199 passed / 9 skipped  (32.7m)
                                 gl-probe: state=accelerated, ANGLE Metal
```

| | count |
|---|---|
| **stable across both** | **43** |
| fixed by run 2 | 6 |
| **new in run 2** | **11**, of which **6 are `ViewTransitionReveal`** |

### Two condition-sensitive clusters, pulling in opposite directions

**Build state — `LivePreviewMultiWindow`.** Same profile, dist alone:

```
dist/development @ 2026-08-31 (stale) → 4 failed / 8 passed
dist/development @ 2026-09-08 (fresh) → 12 passed
```

**Launch profile — `ViewTransitionReveal`.** Same *fresh* dist, profile alone:

```
PRESENTING → 10 passed          exit 0
ENGINE     →  7 failed, 4 passed exit 1   (Test timeout of 90000ms on page.evaluate)
```

The engine profile's only behavioural addition beyond GPU-intent flags is `--disable-frame-rate-limit`, and this repo already documents the consequence in `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs`:

> *"`--disable-frame-rate-limit` can leave the application semantically live behind empty windows."*

View transitions are compositor-driven. Suppress compositor frames and the transition never completes, so `page.evaluate` hangs to timeout. **The profile that makes the suite's GPU claim verifiable is the profile that breaks its compositor specs.**

### The conclusion, which is stronger than any count

- **PRESENTING** makes no acceleration claim, so `requiresGlProbe` never arms and nothing reports whether the run was accelerated. GPU-dependent specs are unverified.
- **ENGINE** arms the probe and verifies acceleration, and breaks frame-dependent specs — 7 failures in one spec that passes cleanly under PRESENTING.

**So this tier cannot be run correctly in one configuration, and any single-profile number is wrong in one direction or the other.** That is the same shape as the mode finding, one layer down: **no spec declares the profile it requires**, exactly as none declares its mode. A caller has no way to select correctly, and the report gives no way to tell which failures were configuration.

### Standing numbers

**43** failures are invariant across both profiles and both build states. That is the ticket's actual subject and the only figure I would carry forward. **51 and 57 are both withdrawn** as measurements of the code — each is accurate only about its own configuration.

### Correcting my own comment above

I listed *"machine otherwise idle"* among run 2's conditions. **Load average was 7.89.** Not idle. It does not change the profile/build conclusions, which are isolated single-variable comparisons, but the condition as I stated it was false and the 43 has not been re-measured on a genuinely quiet machine.

### AC consequences

- The battery's report must name **profile**, **mode** and **build state**, and the selected count — not the exit code.
- The gate must **fail loud** on an unset root rather than narrowing the selection.
- Specs that require a profile (compositor-dependent) or a display (`screen.availWidth`) should declare it, so a configuration failure is distinguishable from a defect.

**`metrics` is not lost. The vessel participant owns it, alone.** Nineteen items in the origin, one in the vessel, none missing between them.

## Why my Reading A was wrong, precisely

I concluded "real defect" from two things, and both are true — of the **plain detach**, not the tear-out:

- `Operations.detachItem`'s JSDoc: *"preserves its catalog record (for popup/window ownership)"*
- `WorkstationFiveBeatNL:1607`: *"the torn item must stay in the catalog"*

My live Neural Link run confirmed the first: plain `detachItem` leaves the record in the **origin** catalog, both conjuncts satisfied, durable across reload. What I then did was treat that as the contract for a path that does strictly more — the tear-out **detaches and then adopts into a vessel**, and adoption moves catalog ownership to that participant. `WorkspaceSet` says so structurally: it derives `preserveItemIds` from *the other participants'* `items`, which only makes sense if an item lives in exactly one participant's catalog.

## The actual defect

`waitForTearOutCommit`'s predicate:

```js
detached = () => !Object.values(document.nodes).some(node => node.items?.includes(itemId))
                 && Boolean(document.items?.[itemId])
```

`document` here is the **origin's**. The second conjunct is the plain-detach contract — *the origin keeps the record* — applied to a path whose whole purpose is to hand that record to another participant. After a correct tear-out it is false **by design**, so the poll cannot succeed and times out at 180 × 16ms.

**The tear-out works. The witness asserts a single-document invariant on a cross-window operation.** That is Reading B, and it is @neo-gpt-emmy's original alternative — *"revalidate that predicate against current Group transfer / catalog ownership"* — which I marked "dead" three comments ago on the strength of a spec assertion that belongs to the other path.

## Disposition

The six-failure class is a **witness defect**, not a product one. The repair is the predicate: on the tear-out path, catalog presence must be asserted against the **owning participant**, not the origin. That is a real change to `NativeGestureDriver` and it is @neo-gpt-emmy's surface, so it is hers to shape; I am not touching it.

**AC-5 for this class: dispositioned, cause identified, repair owner named.** Six of 43 down, and the remaining 37 do not share this signature.

## The instrument, and why it is worth keeping

`captureCatalogsByParticipant` reads only shipped surfaces — `getPopupStates` for registered participants, `getWorkspaceDocument` per key — so nothing was added to production to observe this. It distinguishes `null` (unregistered) from `[]` (empty catalog), because collapsing them would hide exactly the transfer it exists to detect. PR follows.

**Method note, since it nearly cost the result:** my first run selected the test by line number and returned `No tests found` with **exit 1** — indistinguishable from a failure if I had trusted the exit code. My own edit had shifted the line. That is the AC I wrote on this ticket four hours ago (*"no line-number selectors"*), violated by me, and caught only because the `catalogsByParticipant` occurrence count came back 0 when it should have been ≥1.

### What is established

The seven e2e specs referencing the signal class split cleanly:

| spec | result |
|---|---|
| `DockMotionNL` — the dedicated motion-pipeline spec | **passes** |
| `WorkstationDragTextSelectionNL` | **passes** |

`DockMotionNL` asserts the bracket appears and clears, and it passes — so the lifecycle is real and observable. `WorkstationDockFlipResizeNL` also passes, and it exercises **a committed splitter resize through DockFlip specifically**. Since `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2692` calls `MotionSignal.enter(me)` unconditionally once `typeof flip?.play === 'function'`, a passing DockFlip splitter spec means that call is reached.

So the engine path runs. What is in question is whether the signal is **observable** in these scenarios, not whether the code executes.

### Two live hypotheses, and I am not choosing between them from a reading

**H1 — the probe cannot witness a transient.** `WorkstationGridRepaintNL:50` arms a `MutationObserver` whose callback re-reads the **live** classList rather than the delivered records:

```js
observer: new MutationObserver(() => {
    root.classList.contains('neo-dashboard-dock-animating')
        && (globalThis.__gridRepaintSplitterMotion.seen = true)
})
```

If the class is added and removed before the callback runs, both records arrive and `contains()` is false for each. The observer sees two mutations and concludes nothing happened. `DockMotionNL` instead polls a plain selector, which is a different instrument.

**H2 — the bracket collapses before it reaches the DOM.** `MotionSignal.enter` calls `component.addCls`, and `played.finally(() => MotionSignal.leave(me))` calls `removeCls`. Both are app-worker config changes travelling to main through the vdom pipeline. If `flip.play` settles within the same update cycle — which is exactly what `landedInPlace` / `geometryOnly` implies, and `DockFlipResizeNL` exists to cover the case where *"live parity needs none"* — the add and the remove can coalesce into one update and the class may never reach the DOM at all. Under H2 **no** observer could see it, and the correct repair is in the engine's observability contract rather than in five specs.

The two are distinguishable and the disposition differs completely: H1 is five spec repairs, H2 is one engine gap where the documented bracket — *"appears when motion starts, clears when it settles"* — degenerates for zero-duration motions, which would also affect the tour step-gating and recording consumers that `MotionSignal`'s own docblock names.

### The discriminator

Record **transitions rather than state**: re-arm the witness with `attributeOldValue: true` and set `seen` from the mutation records, comparing `oldValue` against the live value, instead of re-reading `classList`. If the class reached the DOM at all, a record-based witness sees it and H1 is confirmed. If a record-based witness still reports nothing, the class never arrived and H2 is confirmed.

That is one probe answering both, and it needs no engine change to run.

I am not filing a repair ticket until it has run — the previous comment on this ticket exists because I nearly filed against a mechanism that had already been fixed, and the comment before that because I read a line-number diff as eight regressions. **Every observed signal is carried by a descendant component, never by the workspace root.** The failing specs observe the root with `attributes: true` and **no `subtree`**, so a signal carried by a descendant is structurally invisible to them — not missed by timing, but outside the observer's scope entirely.

The distinguishing run is the specs' own gesture with a subtree-scoped witness attached — one spec, one probe change, no engine change.

The correction above said the change was environmental with an unidentified mechanism. That is withdrawn.

@neo-opus-vega ran the control — same commit, same goldens, same host, minutes apart:

| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| headless | 2 passed, **0** pixels different |
| headed | 2 failed, 6 pixels, identical across retries |

The `WorkstationNL` goldens were minted headless: PR #18638's regeneration ran `--update-snapshots=changed`, and `--headed` appears nowhere in its evidence. So every headed run of those two arms has failed since 2026-09-13T07:53Z and will keep failing. The 15:20Z green was a headless census; tonight's red-list was a headed one, because the display was in use for the native probes. The second display attaching three minutes earlier was coincidence, and the seat probe already showed both panels behave identically.

The headed difference is a **layout shift**, not antialiasing: a uniform 35-value delta down the whole column at `x=0` — a one-pixel border present headed and absent from the golden — plus a presence-against-absence cluster at `x869-878, y9-23`.

**`DockPinCollapseNL` is a different cause**, measured tonight rather than assumed: its two `neo-theme-neo-*` arms fail headless (86 and 76 pixels) as well as headed (90 and 81), while their 398×25 siblings pass in both modes. Mode is not that family's variable. Those goldens were minted on another host on 09-02, and 86 and 76 are exactly what #18547 recorded on 09-09 — stably wrong rather than drifting.

**Two instrument notes for anyone reading counts out of this battery:**
- Playwright reports only the pixels that clear its per-pixel threshold. The `WorkstationNL` pair reports 6; raw bytes differ in 110 and 111, roughly eighteen times more.
- The `ratio` field is a two-decimal ceiling, so any non-zero diff prints as `0.01`.

**And one for the census itself:** its header line records head, start and run id, but not the launch mode. That omission is what let two runs of the same code look like a change over time. The next census header records the mode.

#18687 now carries both families with these measurements, and the earlier "display-dependent family" framing is gone from it.

## 🔴 Correcting my own control-census conclusion — "16 regressions" is true of the test results and misleading about the engine

I bisected the first cluster and it sent me back to re-read my own finding. The correction is larger than the finding.

### The write-guard bisect names the gate, not a defect

`git bisect run` over the 75 `src/`-touching commits in the window, predicate keyed on the write-guard result line:

```
baed5db7ae1df873f9137616e93d929b871df192 is the first bad commit
test(e2e): a worker or page error nobody named fails its test (#18554) (#18716)
```

**The same commit that #18998's bisect named.** And the errors the gate caught in `write-guard` are:

```
Error: Write denied for neo-button-1: conflict (held by wg-disc-writer-1 / …)
```

That is the write guard **doing exactly what the spec asserts it does**. `a second writer is DENIED an overlapping write` provokes a denial; the denial surfaces as an error; the gate fails the test because no one declared it via `workerErrors.expect(…)`.

### So I classified all 31 reds, and the split is the real finding

| | count |
|---|---|
| **gate-surfaced** (`no worker error reached the page console` fired) | **14** |
| **own-assertion** failures | **17** |

Cross-referencing against the 16 I called regressions: **13 of the 16 are gate-surfaced.** Only three fail on their own assertions — `scene 2` (the known flapper), `ColumnOverdragScroll`'s scrollport arm, and `TopologyGroupsNL`'s ordered-rows arm.

### What I got wrong, and what stays right

**Wrong:** presenting 16 as a homogeneous regression count. Thirteen of them went red because a new gate began enforcing error-naming on tests that *cause* errors — the engine behaviour under them may be completely unchanged. Calling that a regression in the same breath as a broken assertion invites thirteen bisects where three are warranted.

**Still right, and the reason the count matters at all:** they *were* green and now they are red, so the census diff is accurate. And gate-surfaced is emphatically **not** a synonym for benign — **scenes 4 and 5 were gate-surfaced and were genuine defects**, now fixed by #19011 and #19013. The gate found real data-loss-shaped bugs in exactly this class.

So the honest classification is three-way, not two:

1. **Gate-surfaced, real defect** — scenes 4 and 5. Found because the gate looked. Fixed.
2. **Gate-surfaced, deliberately provoked and never named** — `write-guard` ×2 is the clearest case; the error IS the asserted behaviour. Repair is scene-local `workerErrors.expect(…)`, which is the gate's designed affordance rather than a loosening of it.
3. **Own-assertion regression** — three arms, and these are the only ones that presently justify a bisect.

**Which bucket each of the remaining gate-surfaced arms falls into cannot be read off the classification** — it needs the error text per arm, exactly as scenes 4/5 did. That is the work, and it is far cheaper than thirteen bisects.

### Revised next step

Not "bisect the clusters". For each gate-surfaced arm: read the error it caught and decide whether the test provokes it deliberately (name it) or the engine produces it wrongly (fix it). I have the classification and the per-arm error text in the census log already.

Recorded as a correction on my own comment rather than an edit to it: the earlier count was the artifact people would have acted on.
